missing_concepts: Simplex tableau structure: every row except the last represents one constraint's coefficients for the decision and slack variables plus its right-hand-side constant; the last row represents the objective equation, written so the objective variable (here P) has coefficient 1 and the row's right-hand side is the objective's current value.

Basic versus nonbasic variables: a variable is basic in a simplex tableau when its column is a unit vector (a single 1 in exactly one row and 0 in every other row, including the objective row); every nonbasic variable is set to 0 when reading off the current solution.

Entering-variable rule (most-negative-coefficient rule): in a maximization tableau whose objective row is written as -c1*y1 - c2*y2 - ... + P = (current P), the entering variable is the nonbasic variable with the most negative objective-row coefficient, because that column offers the greatest rate of increase in the objective per unit increase of that variable.

Minimum-ratio test (leaving-variable rule): for the chosen entering column, divide each constraint row's right-hand-side by that row's entry in the entering column wherever the entry is positive; the row that gives the smallest nonnegative ratio is the pivot row, and its currently basic variable leaves the basis; this rule keeps every variable nonnegative after the pivot.

Pivot operation mechanics: divide every entry in the pivot row by the pivot element so the pivot position becomes 1, then, for every other row (including the objective row), subtract that row's entering-column entry times the new pivot row from itself, so every other entry in the entering column becomes 0.

Optimality criterion: a maximization tableau in the -c_j convention is optimal exactly when every entry in the objective row under the decision- and slack-variable columns is greater than or equal to 0; any remaining negative entry means a further pivot on that column could still increase the objective.

Reading a basic feasible solution from a tableau: after any pivot, each basic variable's value equals the right-hand-side entry of the row in which it is basic, each nonbasic variable equals 0, and the objective's current value equals the right-hand-side entry of the objective row.
recommended_changes: Add a linear algebra or operations-research source book to the corpus that teaches the simplex method (tableau setup, pivoting, entering and leaving variable rules, optimality criteria, reading basic feasible solutions); the current one-book corpus (single-variable OpenStax Calculus Volume 1) has zero coverage of this skill family and no in-corpus fix is possible.

Until such a book is added, keep no_primary_available true and do not promote openstax_calculus_v1 Sec 4.7 (Applied Optimization Problems) to PRIMARY or SUPPORTING: it solves single-variable optimization by substitution and critical points, a materially different method from the simplex tableau this problem tests.
